author: doughowe
body:
* **UniProt Keyword ID and label:**
KW-0816 Tricarboxylic acid cycle

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
ZDB-GENE-130530-761        ugl (ureidoglycolate lyase)

* **Description of issue**
PMID:37043539
This paper shows that zebrafish ugl lacks malate synthase activity and is therefore not in the TCA cycle but instead it has ureiodoglycolate lyase activity and is therefor in the glyoxylate cycle.  Currently KW-0816 is mapping zebrafish ugl to GO:0006099 (tricarboxylic acid cycle), when it should not.
title: Incorrect UniProt KW mapping:  KW-0816 Tricarboxylyc acid cycle to zebrafish ugl gene

author: Antonialock
source_title: InterPro2GO issue:  IPR006252 and IPR001465 are giving zebrafish ugl malate sythase activity incorrectly

author: Antonialock
body: I annotated the protein to EC=4.3.2.3 CC PATHWAY: Purine metabolism; urate degradation {EXP|Ref.2} FUNCTION: Catalyzes the last step of purine degradation by converting ureidoglycolate into glyoxylate and urea based on fig 7 + enzyme assays in the paper.

author: Antonialock
body:
@doughowe It looks like glyoxylate cycle is downstream and only includes isocitrate lyase and malate synthase e.g. DEF: A modification of the TCA cycle occurring in some plants and microorganisms, in which isocitrate is cleaved to glyoxylate and succinate. Glyoxylate can then react with acetyl-CoA to form malate. 

What do you think?
